title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing Notes (2028-07)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document summarizes the Unified Inference product surface (overview + PRD), design constraints, roadmap and themes through Q4 2028, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the 2028-07 planning window. It is intended for PMs, engineering leads, sales enablement, and finance to align on scope, success metrics, and commercial packaging.

Key takeaways
- Unified Inference continues to be Redwood's single API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- This release focuses on two goals: 1) reduce per-token unit economics for cold-start and short-turn workloads, and 2) make routing/variant controls first-class for customers (policy UI + API).
- Pricing update proposal: introduce a latency-tiered per-token band and a routing surcharge for cross-region fallbacks. See Pricing & Packaging section.

1) Product overview and problem statement

Background
- Customers operate a mix of usage patterns: long-form generation (high tokens/session), low-latency chat (short tokens, tight P99), and batch embedding workloads.
- Historically customers trade latency vs cost by selecting model families or toggling quantization. Operability suffers when fallbacks or heterogeneous model variants are used across regions.

Problem statement
- Customers want predictable unit economics while keeping latency SLOs. They also want simple controls to define routing/fallback behavior between models and hardware classes without writing custom proxies.

Solution (high-level)
- Unified Inference exposes per-route policy controls + cost-aware auto-routing. Customers can:
  - Pin a route to a model version and fallback chain.
  - Choose latency tiers (low, medium, best-effort) which influence routing and pricing.
  - Apply cost caps and automatic quantization profiles per-route.

2) PRD: requirements and success metrics

Goals (MUST)
1. Per-route latency tiers: low (P99 < 150ms short requests), medium (P99 < 400ms), best-effort (no P99 SLO).
2. Cost-aware routing engine that selects model variant+deployment to meet tier with minimal estimated cost.
3. Admin UI and API to configure route policies, fallback chains, and cost caps.
4. Billing attribution per-route and per-fallback event (to support the routing surcharge).

Non-goals (WON'T)
- Replace customer-side traffic shaping or full runtime orchestration for model training pipelines.

Success metrics
- Adoption: 25% of new production routes created in the quarter use latency tiers.
- Cost reduction: average per-token cost for short-session chat workload reduced by 18% within 60 days of rollout for participating customers.
- Reliability: routing fallback incidents should be < 0.5% of requests and have <1 minute mean time to automatic fallback.

Requirements table
| ID | Type | Requirement | Owner | Priority | Notes |
|-----|------|-------------|-------|---------|-------|
| R1 | Functional | Per-route latency tiers (API + UI) | product | Must | tiers: low/medium/best-effort |
| R2 | Functional | Cost-aware routing engine (service: routing-engine) | eng-serving-runtime | Must | integrates with capacity signals |
| R3 | Functional | Billing attribution for fallbacks | finance | Must | invoice line-item support |
| R4 | UX | Policy editor with validation and test harness | eng-developer-experience | Should | live preview for routing decisions |
| R5 | Security | RBAC controls for route changes | security-and-compliance | Must | audit logging required |

3) Design specs and architecture notes

Architecture summary
- New components: routing-engine (stateless), policy-store (config DB), policy-evaluator (library in runtime), and policy-ui (console).
- flow: request -> api-gateway -> policy-evaluator -> routing-engine decision -> chosen-runtime-endpoint

Design constraints
- Policy evaluation must be sub-ms added latency in the hot path; prefer cached compiled policies and tiered TTLs.
- Decisions must be deterministic for identical inputs to ensure reproducible debugging and billing.
- Fallbacks must carry metadata to credit billing and observability (original-route, evaluated-policy-id, decision-reason).

Example JSON policy (reference)
{
  "policy_id": "chat-low-latency-v1",
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "tier": "low",
  "fallback_chain": ["chat-xlarge-quant", "chat-large-quant"],
  "cost_cap_usd_per_hour": "50",
  "rules": [
    {"if": {"region": "eu"}, "prefer": "eu-optimized"}
  ]
}

(Implementation note: policy JSON above is a developer-facing reference. The policy-store schema will be normalized in the first implementation sprint.)

Observability and telemetry
- Emit routing_decision events (fields: request_id, policy_id, chosen_variant, latency_est_ms, estimated_cost_micros, decision_time_ms, fallback_hops).
- Dashboard: per-route cost breakdown, P50/P95/P99 latencies, fallback rate, and token counts.

4) Roadmap & themes (Q3 2028 -> Q4 2028)

Roadmap milestones
- Q3 2028 (Jul-Sep): policy-store MVP, API for latency tiers, console policy editor (alpha), and routing-engine prototype. Internal dogfood with two enterprise customers.
- Q4 2028 (Oct-Dec): GA of latency tiers + routing UI, billing attribution for fallbacks, runtime integrations across Dedicated pool and Private deployments, and first pricing update effective 2028-11-01.

Themes and tradeoffs
- Theme: Cost-aware defaults. Tradeoff: defaults should save cost but not silently degrade subjective quality — use canary rollouts and per-route quality monitoring.
- Theme: Predictability at scale. Tradeoff: more conservative routing decisions increase cost. Provide fine-grained knobs.

Dependencies and risks
- Dependency on eng-infra for capacity signals and cost telemetry hooks.
- Risk: inaccurate cost model leads to frequent fallback thrashing; mitigation: ramp policies with rate limits and dry-run mode.

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing changes proposed (summary)
- Introduce latency-tiered per-token prices for generation requests (hosted only initially):
  - low-latency tier: +15% over base per-token price (applies when customers select 'low' tier)
  - medium: base price (no change)
  - best-effort: -10% discount off base price
- Introduce a routing-fallback surcharge: $0.0001 per-fallback-event for cross-region fallback decisions (intended to recapture egress + routing costs).
- Dedicated/Private: pricing will be exposed as capacity adjustment + feature flag (per-route policy support included in enterprise tier).

Packaging guidance
- Self-serve: latency tiers and best-effort discount available in hosted self-serve.
- Enterprise add-on: advanced policy controls (rate-limited rollouts, audit retention, private policy-store replicants) are included in Dedicated/Private packages.
- Migration incentives: customers that opt-in to route-level cost caps and dry-run policies get 10% credit on their first month of increased usage (requires enrollment).

Billing and metric mapping
- billing_line_item: route_latency_tier, routing_fallback_count, tokens_generated, tokens_embedded
- billing dashboards must show estimated vs actual cost for the month.

6) Release notes (planned for GA in 2028-11)

Release 2028-07 (internal dogfood)
- Added policy-store MVP and API.
- Console: policy editor alpha with validation.
- Routing-engine prototype deployed to internal cluster; dogfooding with 2 customers.
- Observability: added routing_decision events to the event bus.

Planned release 2028-11 (GA)
- GA: per-route latency tiers (low/medium/best-effort).
- GA: policy UI and API for configuring fallback chains and cost caps.
- Billing: route-level attribution enabled with experimental invoice fields.
- Pricing change: latency-tier pricing effective 2028-11-01 for new customers (existing customers get 60 days notice).

Operational playbook (brief)
1. Enable feature flag: policy-routing-v1 for target orgs.
2. Run dry-run for 2 weeks to collect decision telemetry.
3. Monitor fallback rate and per-route cost. Thresholds: if fallback_rate > 1% or estimated_cost increase > 25% over baseline, rollback policy or narrow scope.
4. Escalation: paging to eng-platform on sustained failure > 10 minutes and to product for customer communications.

Open questions for leadership
- What is the acceptable baseline surcharge for cross-region fallbacks for large enterprise customers?
- Should the latency-tiered pricing be gated behind usage bands (e.g., > $5k monthly) or offered to all customers?

Appendix: implementation sprint plan (high level)
- Sprint 1 (4 weeks): policy schema, policy-store + API, basic console editor, unit tests.
- Sprint 2 (4 weeks): routing-engine integration, runtime policy-evaluator, event telemetry. Dry-run with internal traffic.
- Sprint 3 (4 weeks): billing integration, enterprise RBAC, dogfood with 2 customers.
- Sprint 4 (4 weeks): GA polish, pricing rollout coordination, docs and sales enablement.
